Definition: from G2596 and G2983; to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively):--apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take.
BiblicalUsage: To take hold is to seize and to understand at once, and John says the light shines in darkness and the darkness comprehended it not. Paul says he presses on to apprehend that for which he was apprehended, and he prays we may comprehend the breadth and length and depth and height of Christ's love. The word is both a grip and a grasp of the mind, and the race is run to lay hold of the prize.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Christ took hold of me first, and that is why I press on to take hold of Him. I hold that the love of Christ is wider than I can measure and still worth measuring, and the race is worth running because the prize is Him.
RelatedTopics: Light and Darkness; Perseverance; Love of God
